title: Scalars vs vectors
examples: What is the difference between speed and velocity?
If I walk north and then east, how do I find my final position?
Can you show me how to add two vectors using a diagram?

explain.say: Today we learn about scalars and vectors. Some physical quantities need only a size. Others need a size and a direction.
A scalar quantity has only magnitude. Magnitude just means a size or a number. For example, temperature is a scalar quantity.
A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. You must state the direction to be correct. Force is a common example of a vector.

draw.text: Vector: Size AND Direction (e.g., Force, Velocity)

explain.say: To add vectors, we use a method called the resultant. We draw them head to tail on a diagram. The final vector is the resultant.

items: The final vector is the resultant

explain.say: Imagine walking three metres east, then two metres north. The resultant is a vector pointing northeast. Its magnitude is the total distance.

faq.q: What is the difference between distance and displacement?
faq.a: Distance is a scalar, meaning it only has magnitude. Displacement is a vector, needing both magnitude and direction. For example, walking around a field covers distance but returns you to zero displacement.
asks: What is the difference between total distance and displacement?

faq.q: When do I need to worry about direction?
faq.a: You need direction when the quantity describes movement or influence. Things like wind force or your final push need a direction to be fully described.
asks: Do all forces have a direction?
When is direction important in physics?

faq.q: How do I add two vectors if they are in the same line?
faq.a: If the vectors are in a straight line, you simply add or subtract their magnitudes. If they are in opposite directions, the smaller one subtracts from the larger one.
asks: If I push right and then left, what do I do?
How do I add vectors along a line?

faq.q: Is speed a vector or a scalar?
faq.a: Speed is a scalar because it only tells you how fast you are going. Velocity, which includes speed and direction, is the vector.
asks: What is the vector version of speed?
Can you give me an example of a scalar speed?

faq.a: The resultant is the single vector that represents the overall effect of two or more individual vectors acting together. It is the final, combined vector.
asks: What is the final vector after adding forces?
How do I find the resultant force?

facts: Mass is a scalar quantity because it only has magnitude.
Velocity is a vector quantity because it requires both magnitude and direction.
When adding vectors, the resultant represents the overall net effect.
Displacement is a vector, while distance is a scalar.

quiz.say: Which of these quantities is a scalar: speed, force, or momentum?
quiz.why: Speed only has magnitude, making it a scalar quantity.

wrong.0: Momentum is also a vector, requiring both size and direction.
wrong.1: Mass is a scalar, but speed is the best example given.
wrong.3: Force is a vector because it must have a direction applied.

quiz.say: If you walk four metres due north and then two metres due east, what is the resultant vector?
quiz.why: The resultant is found by drawing the vectors head to tail, giving a direction.

wrong.0: The answer must be a vector because direction is important here.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the magnitudes without considering the direction.
wrong.3: This lists the components but does not give the single resultant vector.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes adding two vectors?
quiz.why: The head-to-tail method is the standard way to find the resultant of multiple vectors.

wrong.1: Multiplication is not the correct mathematical operation for vector addition.
wrong.2: This ignores the crucial element of direction in vector sums.
wrong.3: If you treat them as scalars, you lose the directional information needed.
